title: genai third-party scorer deserialization: match the module allow-list exactly and validate metric_name and kwargs before any import
answers: Why does loading a registered RAGAS, DeepEval, TruLens or Phoenix scorer fail with 'not in the allow-list' when it was saved from a run artifact path?
How are third-party scorer class and metric_name checked before MLflow imports the module when rebuilding a scorer from stored data?
Where is the allow-list of scorer modules for third-party scorer deserialization defined and enforced?
What happens if a scorer payload sets kwargs to include metric_name, or a dotted metric_name?
body:
Path: Rebuilding a third-party scorer (ragas, deepeval, trulens, phoenix) from a stored `third_party_scorer_data` payload goes through `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py:Scorer.model_validate`, which reads module, class, metric_name and kwargs and then calls `importlib.import_module`. The allow-list is `mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py:THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES`.
Rule: Allow-list membership is exact string equality against the 14 scorer-defining modules (the four package roots plus their `scorers` submodules), never a package-prefix or `startswith` match. Checks run before any import: module is in the frozenset, `metric_name.isidentifier()`, and `"metric_name"` is not a key of kwargs. After `getattr`, the resolved object must be `inspect.isclass` and a `Scorer` subclass before instantiation. Any new scorer-defining module must be added to the frozenset explicitly.
Symptom: A file placed below an allow-listed package (for example a run artifact under a `file://` experiment artifact root, resolved as `mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens.<run_id>.artifacts.payload`) was importable, so its top-level code ran before the class or metric-name checks.
Constraints: MLflow's own serializers always emit the defining module, so registered scorers from any release still load; only hand-built paths that no serializer emits are rejected. No public API or payload schema changes. Applies to `Scorer.model_validate` third-party branch only, not to built-in judges or `@scorer` functions.
applies: Scorer deserialization of third-party scorer payloads in mlflow/genai/scorers; any change to which modules or metric_name/kwargs values a stored scorer may carry.
says: Loading an external evaluation metric stored under experiment run artifacts fails validation.
Block untrusted code execution when reopening saved third party evaluators from artifact storage.
Evaluation runs fail to restore when metric names contain periods or invalid characters.
Stored evaluation metrics fail to load if configuration parameters conflict with metric names.
search: Third-party scorer deserialization in mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py:Scorer.model_validate validates module against mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py:THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES using exact string equality before importing. Prior to importlib.import_module, it verifies metric_name.isidentifier() and ensures metric_name is not in kwargs, then checks that the resolved attribute is a Scorer subclass. This prevents importing arbitrary files under artifact roots while preserving loading of legitimate registered scorers, and does not apply to built-in judges or @scorer functions.
